title: On the Role of Anticausal Direction in LLM-based Data Synthesis

problem.claim: The study investigates whether the direction of LLM-based synthetic data generation affects synthetic data quality and downstream utility.

gap.claim: Existing LLM-based data synthesis workflows are mostly anticausal, contrasting with the natural causal direction of data synthesis.

contributions.claim: Constructs paired causal and anticausal synthetic datasets for five tasks and evaluates them through supervised fine-tuning and post-training.
Reports that models trained on causal synthetic data consistently outperform models trained on anticausal synthetic data.
Proposes XSyn, a generative framework that transforms causal and anticausal synthetic data toward real-world distributions using four reward models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across five tasks, models trained on causal synthetic data consistently outperform those trained on anticausal data.
Experiments on BERT, Llama, and Qwen report substantial gains from training on XSyn-transformed data over causal and anticausal counterparts.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are increasingly used to generate synthetic data.
Most workflows use an anticausal direction that contrasts with the natural causal direction of data synthesis.
The study constructs paired datasets across five tasks and evaluates models trained on them.
Models trained on causal synthetic data reportedly outperform those trained on anticausal data.
The authors propose XSyn and report gains from XSyn-transformed data across several model families.

source_observation.claim: Causal synthetic data reportedly produces better downstream model performance than anticausal synthetic data across five tasks.

interpretation.claim: The direction used to organize synthetic data generation may affect its usefulness for downstream training.

application.claim: When designing LLM-based data synthesis workflows, compare causal and anticausal generation directions for the target task.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported direction effect generalizes beyond the five evaluated tasks.

source_observation.claim: XSyn-transformed data reportedly outperforms both causal and anticausal counterparts in experiments on BERT, Llama, and Qwen.

interpretation.claim: Transforming synthetic data toward real-world distributions may improve its downstream utility.

application.claim: Synthetic-data pipelines may benefit from reward-guided transformations aimed at matching real-world distributions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the magnitude, task-specificity, or robustness of the reported gains.

unknowns: No dataset sizes, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results are provided.
No details are given about the four reward models or XSyn optimization procedure.
No information is provided about statistical significance, ablations, or limitations.
